name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 5, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at 5:00
p.m., on April 5, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 31, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are

City Council Minutes  1  April 5, 2010
   the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD), Case No. 30-2009-
  00300610.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session items CS1, the City Council
provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

For item CS2, staff gave an update on the denial of a motion by the Saddleback Valley Unified
School District (in court today) but there was nothing further to report.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winner

  Mayor Kelley and Michelle Clark from Waste Management presented the recycling
  award to residents Del and Leslie Holt.

P2.  Recognition of Home Delivered Meal Volunteers and Congregate Meal Volunteers
  from the Norman P. Murray Center and Community Center

  Mayor Kelley presented Certificates of Appreciation to Marilyn Ditty, Executive Director
  of Age Well Senior Services, Inc.

P3.  Presentation by the Orange County Transportation Authority Regarding the "Go
  Local" Transit Program

  Richard Dial of HDR and Steven Wilks of the IBI Group (on behalf of OCTA) gave a
  presentation on the “Go Local” Transit Program.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Teryll Hopper, Community and Legislative Affairs Director for the Orange County Association

City Council Minutes  2  April 5, 2010
 of Realtors, Dana Point: stated that the Orange County Association of Realtors is concerned with
Measure D and they will actively work to oppose the measure.

Frank Barron, M.V.: asked the City Council to help support the award-winning Mission Viejo
High School band program through suggestions, public funding, donations, or grants.

F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: stated that he supports anything the City can do to help the Mission
Viejo High School music program. Mr. Holtzman also discussed the state of city's streets and
recommended that funds be earmarked for street repairs.

Linda Wolter, M.V.: stated that she enjoys living in Mission Viejo but she was disappointed that
the animal shelter did not grant her an interview to volunteer with cats due to her physical
disabilities.

Barbara Anderson, M.V.: stated that the raider trailers on Montanoso have been very successful
in slowing traffic. She suggested placing permanent radar signs in combination with curb
extensions to help with speed issues on that street.

Linda Barnes, M.V.: invited City Council Members and staff to the California Water Crisis
Conference at Irvine Valley College Performing Arts Center on Sunday, April 25, 2010, at 2:00
p.m.

Wendy Bucknum, South Orange County Regional Chambers of Commerce, M.V.: stated that the
Chamber of Commerce is opposed to Measure D because it imposes too many restrictions on the
city’s businesses and property owners.

Frank Lieberman, M.V.: reminded residents that the 12th Annual Fun With Chalk street painting
festival will be held on April 24 and 25, 2010, at the Murray Community Center along with the
Arts Alive festival. He also thanked City Manager Dennis Wilberg for his support over the
years.

Bob Bruchmann, M.V.: stated that the Saddleback Republican Assembly rejected his application
for membership because he does not agree with them on certain issues.

Michelle Clark, Waste Management: reminded residents that Waste Management will donate, to
the Mission Viejo Library, $5 for every ton of recyclable material collected during the month of
April.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed the text that an Orange County Superior Court Judge ordered to
be removed from Council Member Ury’s Argument Against Measure D.

Kate Keena, M.V.: expressed opposition to Measure D and stated that it has a huge potential for
hurting business in Mission Viejo and she feels it is a strong abuse of the election process.

City Council Minutes  3  April 5, 2010
 Vickie Talley, Southern California Chapter of the National Association of Industrial and Office
Properties (NAIOP), Laguna Hills: stated that she represents commercial real estate owners
within the city and last week, the Board of Directors of NAIOP took an official position to
oppose Measure D and they urge the citizens of Mission Viejo to vote no.

Marvis Kusanick, M.V.: discussed parking problems at the civic center and requested that the
Council consider converting the court yard area to a one-way street. She further questioned the
number of reserved spaces for city staff and suggested the Park and Ride participants use the
outer parking lot.

Terry Yapp, M.V.: speaking as an elected Director of the Orange County Association of Realtors
and as a Mission Viejo resident and property owner, he expressed his opposition to Measure D
and stated that it is poor public policy and he will do everything he can to defeat the measure.

Dan Avery, M.V.: stated that Measure D seriously challenges the quality of life in Mission Viejo
and he encouraged residents to vote no on the measure.

The following resident presented a written comment in opposition to Measure D: Nancy Cho,
M.V.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Claim Against the City -- Craig Hooks

  Rejected claim.

4.  Check Register dated March 5, 2010, in the amount of $569,265.14

City Council Minutes  4  April 5, 2010
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated March 12, 2010, in the amount of 1,512,952.72

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register dated March 19, 2010, in the amount of $597,443.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

12.  Speed Humps on Via Santa Maria

  Traffic Engineer Philip Nitollama presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 7:27 p.m., Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing.

  The following spoke in favor of speed humps on Via Santa Maria: Lenore McCormick,
  M.V.; Robert Moncur, M.V.; Brandon Norton, M.V.; Nathan Mercuro, M.V.; and Anna
  T. Boyce, M.V.

  Residents Rob and Cathy McCullough presented a petition containing the signatures of
  27 residents who are in favor of the installation of speed humps on Via Santa Maria.

  At the hour of 7:36 p.m., Mayor Kelley closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  (1) approve the installation of speed humps on Via Santa Maria and (2) adopt Resolution
  10-13 Creating a Parking Restriction on Via Santa Maria.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  5  April 5, 2010
   Council Member Ledesma drew the Council’s attention to item 18, as listed on pages 8
  and 9 of the Minutes. He noted that the Orange County Register erroneously reported
  that he voted against the project but the Minutes accurately reflect his votes. He is in
  favor of the Oso/Marguerite intersection improvements and the pavement rehabilitation
  projects but he voted against the addition of decorative median pilasters and pots on
  pedestals.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of March 15, 2010, as
  presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

7.  Bleacher Shade Covers Project - CIP 321

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that this item came up shortly after the
  Council approved the budget. She stated that the process is not fair and this project
  should have been discussed during the budget workshop. She feels that this takes funds
  from other activities and pits the interests of one person against another. Council
  Member Schlicht stated that she hopes the budget process will be handled in a more
  proactive and fair manner in the future.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to award
  a contract for the subject project to Southern Hemisphere Shades, Inc. in an amount not
  to exceed $103,808.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

Items 8 and 9 were considered together.

8.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract - West Coast Arborists, Inc.

9.  Annual Routine Landscape Maintenance - Contract Area 1

City Council Minutes  6  April 5, 2010
   Speaking for items 8 and 9, Council Member Schlicht stated that change orders are profit
  centers for contractors and the City should have used the competitive bid process one
  year ago.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, (1) to approve the
  Fourth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc. to increase
  the contract in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00 (Agenda item #8); and (2) approved
  the Second Amendment to the existing contract with Nieves Landscape to increase the
  contract in an amount not to exceed $195,000 (Agenda item #9)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

10.  Commercial Food Waste Composting Program

  Council Member Schlicht asked if this program will continue if the City doesn’t qualify
  for grant funding in the future.

  Senior Management Analyst Denise Matson replied that the City would not do the project
  without the grant funding and the money can only be used on very specific projects for
  waste diversion activities. Ms. Matson stated that the program is unique because once the
  equipment is purchased and the grant funds are spent, the food dehydrators will still be in
  place and the program will therefore continue.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve the commercial food waste composting services agreement with Waste
  Management of Orange County in the amount of $400,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

11.  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 (ARRA) Project Updates (CIPs
  202/837, 207 and 320)

  Mayor Kelley announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to highlight
  the monies that the City has received from the Federal Stimulus Program.

City Council Minutes  7  April 5, 2010
   City Manager Dennis Wilberg discussed the projects that the City will complete via the
  grants.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

13.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

14.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

15.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

16.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

Council Member Ledesma vacated the dais at 8:10 p.m. Council Member Ury vacated the dais
at 8:11 p.m. Both Mr. Ledesma and Mr. Ury returned at 8:13 p.m.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:15 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
8:22 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

17.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2009-10

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  8  April 5, 2010
   Robert Bruchmann, M.V.: stated that members of the Saddleback Republican Assembly
  are either directly or indirectly responsible for the budget deficit by promoting an
  unnecessary recall election and the Measure D election which will cost, in total,
  approximately $430,000.

  Elizabeth Grace Treadwill, Vice Chairman of the Cultural Arts Committee, presented a
  written comment in favor of having the Cultural Arts Committee report to the Mission
  Viejo Library.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 10-14 Amending the FY 2009-10 Budget for Adjustments in Certain
  Revenue and Appropriation Accounts and in the Authorized Position Schedule, and (2)
  adopt Resolution 10-15 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule to Modify the
  Classifications for Three Existing Positions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney’s Report

Responding to a question from Council Member Ury, City Attorney Bill Curley outlined the
results of a court proceeding for the challenge to Council Member Ury’s Argument Against
Measure D. The Judge ruled that two sentences and one word be removed from Council
Member Ury’s argument. Mr. Curley noted that the modified argument, the argument in favor of
Measure D, both rebuttal arguments and the City Attorney’s impartial analysis are all posted on
the City’s web site and on the Registrar of Voters web site.

Council Member Schlicht stated that staff denied her access to copies of the waste management
contract proposals and she feels it’s imperative that there is Council oversight so she wishes to
start reviewing the proposals.

Mr. Curley described the process that staff is following based on the Council-approved contract
with consultant Sloan Vazquez. He noted that copies of the proposals will be provided to the
City Council when the Sloan Vazquez review is complete and their recommendation is presented
to the City Council. Unless the Council, as a whole, directs staff to deviate from the process and
release the proposals sooner, staff will continue to follow that course.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  9  April 5, 2010
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma announced his attendance at the ribbon cutting ceremony for Einstein
Brothers Bagels on the corner of Los Alisos and Santa Margarita Parkway. He stated that it is a
very nice restaurant and he encouraged residents to give it a try.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she sued the City because of the misleading, untrue and
false statements that were in the Argument Against Measure D. She incurred her own legal fees
because she could not allow that statement to proceed without taking it to court. She noted that
she made a challenge to the City Clerk, as the Elections Official, and the City Clerk saw nothing
wrong with the argument so Council Member Schlicht challenged it in court and the Judge
removed significant language from the ballot statement. She stated that she would do it all over
again and that $40,000 in City Attorney legal fees is significant so we ought to look at our City
Attorney more closely. Council Member Schlicht announced that there will be a Mission Viejo
Tea Party on April 15, 2010, from 5:00 to 6:30 p.m. at the corner of La Paz and Marguerite. She
has been to a number of these events and it’s gratifying to be with intergenerational participants
who want better government and public participation. She also reminded residents to mark their
calendars for Saturday and Sunday, April 24 and 25, for the Fun With Chalk festival. Referring
back to Measure D, Council Member Schlicht read from a memo dated August 18, 2008, when
Community Development Director Chuck Wilson reported that Sunrise Senior Living was
slowing down its development plans mostly due to a stale development industry and the
uncertainty of receiving city approvals for any concepts and that is what led to the withdrawal of
their proposed project. She also referred to the official Minutes for the Council Meeting of May
4, 2009, when City Manager Wilberg stated that “this information, coupled with the moratorium
on the property, ensures that it will continue as a golf course for the foreseeable future.” Council
Member Schlicht noted that Measure D will give residents a right to vote on zoning changes and
that the golf course is not secure from development and she feels the Judge agreed by striking
language from Council Member Ury’s argument. Council Member Schlicht ended her comments
by reading an article from the Mission Viejo Dispatch blog which outlined the court proceedings
and the wording that the Judge ordered to be removed from the Argument Against Measure D.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury shared one of his favorite quotes which is “you can’t substitute volume for
substance.” He stated that in spite of the Council’s discussion over the last hour, what’s
important is our City and the kids and families who live here. He referred to his attendance at
Bunny Days and a little girl who participated in the cake walk event. The young girl was so
excited and he noted that she probably made a lifetime memory that day. He stated that these
little nuances can put the Council’s arguments into perspective. Council Member Ury also

City Council Minutes  10  April 5, 2010
 discussed his invitation to throw out the first ball when the Lithuanian team played South
Mission Viejo Little League. He thanked the League President John Fahey and the entire Board
for the invitation. It was a lot of fun interacting with people and he recounted his conversation
with the Lithuanian Little League President who was very impressed with the ball fields in
Mission Viejo. Council Member Ury stated that it was an honor to be there and, at the end of the
day, these are the people who have a proper perspective on life.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that he and Mayor Kelley attended the Sheriff’s
Department Medal of Valor luncheon and he was pleased to see four Mission Viejo Deputies
honored for saving the life of a man who was about to jump from a parking structure. He also
announced that Buffalo Wild Wings will be opening in the former El Torito Grill location in
Kaleidoscope. He had the opportunity to tour the restaurant and it will be a great addition to the
City, along with the new Einstein Bagels that he and Council Member Ledesma visited this
morning. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness noted that the highlight of his week was a ride-along with
Code Enforcement Officer Karen Rottmann.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley reminded residents to mark their calendars for the Arts Alive Festival on April 24
and 25, at Oso Viejo Trail and the Village Green. The two-day event will include trail work,
arts, and a joint venture with the Fun With Chalk festival. It will also include the culmination of
the recent Rachel’s Challenge Links of Character program in which students and community
groups have written acts of caring and kindness on paper “chain links.” On April 25, at the Arts
Alive Festival, kids, families, teachers and principals will come together and connect the chains
into a four mile “human chain of kindness.” Mayor Kelley encouraged those who are interested
in participating to contact her for more information. She also elaborated on Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness’ praise of the Police Chief and Deputies who received a life-saving Medal of Valor
award. Due to the heroics and courage of our own Chief of Police Services, Lieutenant Mike
Gavin, Sergeant Rich Himmel and Deputies Wayne Dixon and Edward Macias, the life of a
Mission Viejo man was saved. Mayor Kelley stated that we have guardian angels in all of our
police personnel and she encouraged residents to thank a deputy when they see one. She also
mentioned that a Mission Viejo resident and former Mission Viejo Deputy, Lance Christiansen,
received a Medal of Merit for his social and drug trends education program which is being used
all over the country. Staff at the Capistrano Unified School District nominated Deputy
Christiansen for his work and he has been honored both locally and nationally. Mayor Kelley
stated that she truly has a heart of gratitude knowing that these individuals are out there watching
over Mission Viejo and keeping the city safe. She also announced that the Character Committee
has launched a program called Movies for Character. Each month the committee will present a
movie that reinforces the character quality of the month, beginning with the screening of Pay it
Forward on April 11, 2010, in the Council Chamber. She also discussed her attendance at the
Friends of the Library Foundation meeting and she encouraged residents to purchase a book at
the Friends book store as the money raised in the store supports our library. In addition, Mayor
Kelley attended a recent Chamber of Commerce mixer at Tortilla Flats restaurant. She noted that

City Council Minutes  11  April 5, 2010
 the event was well attended and she was pleased to see the Chamber host an activity like this.
She discussed her attendance at Bunny Days and she announced that the turnout was near 10,000
and this is one of the events that helps to make Mission Viejo special. She also visited the
Einstein Bagels ribbon cutting ceremony and she wished them success. Lastly, Mayor Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of April is service.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:53 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Wayne Lukina, to Monday, April 19, 2010,
at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 19, 2010

City Council Minutes  12  April 5, 2010
